2026-07-03 fix (commit 7dd218aa): GpuAdmissionGate/ExclusiveAdmissionGate used to call get_engine_semaphore("gpu"/"exclusive", 1) in __init__, which shares the SAME registry keyed by engine_class that manifest-derived claims use (e.g. xtts -> "gpu"); since they construct at import time and the registry cached cap at first creation, every GPU-class engine was silently capped at 1 regardless of manifest max_concurrent_workers. Fixed by giving the legacy gates private semaphores and making get_engine_semaphore/EngineClassSemaphore grow-only (ensure_min_cap).

W-PAR 007 Fable-gate fix (2026-07-04): ResourceClaim gained engine_id; new independent get_engine_id_semaphore(engine_id, cap) registry checked ALONGSIDE (never instead of) the per-engine_class semaphore -- prevents one engine's cap from being inflated by a same-class sibling's larger request growing the shared class semaphore (opt-in via engine_id, backward compatible)
EngineClassSemaphore now hard-rejects constructing/growing the 'exclusive' class above cap=1 (ValueError) -- was previously safe by accident, now enforced

Task 014 (2026-07-11): reserve_task_resources resolves the live/effective cap fresh on every call (lazy import of cap_settings.resolve_effective_cap) when a claim carries engine_class/engine_id + manifest_max, passing it as `limit` to try_acquire; a tts_parallel_cap/tts_engine_caps settings change now reaches already-queued and already-running work within one retry cycle instead of requiring a restart.

self._children accessed under self._children_lock (retry swap, heartbeat monitor, active_segments_map aggregation all touch the same list concurrently)

_SyntheticSegmentTask.describe() sets ephemeral=True; ChapterSynthesisTask._publish_progress emits size-weighted, order-independent grouped_progress computed from in-memory child text sizes (count-based progress retained separately)

ChapterSynthesisTask gained an event-driven self._live_segments_map (2026-07-05 escaped-defect fix): _on_child_segment_tick updates it incrementally from each child's own per-tick publish (via the on_segment_tick callback in orchestrator_publish.py), replacing the old completion-boundary sampling that was structurally always empty; _clear_active_segments_map() force-writes an explicit {} at any terminal outcome so a stale mid-render snapshot never rides a terminal frame

ChapterSynthesisTask.run() now calls self._publish_progress(status="running", completed=0, ...) immediately after submitting the ThreadPoolExecutor futures, before the as_completed loop (2026-07-06 fix) -- previously the parent job's own `status` field stayed "preparing" for the ENTIRE first chunk group's render (status only flipped inside as_completed, i.e. only once a whole group COMPLETED).

_on_child_segment_tick(reason_code=None) now derives active_segments_map phase as "preparing" if status=="preparing" OR reason_code in {SEGMENT_PENDING, LOADING_MODEL} else "rendering" (2026-07-06 fix) -- previously hardcoded to "rendering" for every non-terminal tick, so a child's SEGMENT_PENDING/LOADING_MODEL sub-phase (conveyed via reason_code, not status) never surfaced in the map.

2026-07-07 ETA-decay fix: new self._dispatch_eta_seconds instance attr (stashed by orchestrator_helpers.py's _publish_chapter_dispatch_eta before task.run()); new _live_chapter_eta_seconds(status, decay_fraction) decays that dispatch-time estimate by grouped_progress (or plain progress) so the chapter's eta_seconds tracks REMAINING work instead of staying frozen at the t=0 dispatch snapshot; _publish_progress now durably persists status/progress/eta_seconds+active_segments_map via a new update_job(..., skip_job_updated=True) call on every 'running' frame (previously only broadcast via the pure ProgressService.publish(), so the DB row itself went stale between the far-more-frequent map-only update_job writes from _on_child_segment_tick).

2026-07-07 fable-review fixes: (1) eta_seconds is now simply omitted from the update_job(...) call when no dispatch calibration exists, instead of passing explicit None -- an explicit None clears eta_seconds/eta_basis/estimated_end_at at the state layer and would have wiped the ticks' own legitimately-maintained projection-derived ETA at every group boundary; (2) a successful (done/completed) terminal child tick now leaves a transient {phase:'done', progress:1.0, eta_seconds:0} marker in active_segments_map instead of popping the segment -- this is the only live signal keeping a just-finished segment's text lit ahead of the next DB refetch; failed/cancelled terminals still pop unchanged. run()'s as_completed loop now passes status=result.status into _on_child_segment_tick instead of a hardcoded 'done' -- the hardcoded call was a real bug: under the new done-marker semantics it would have permanently mislabeled a failed/cancelled child as successfully rendered. _clear_active_segments_map (unchanged) still force-wipes the whole map at the chapter's own terminal outcome.

Task 008 backend half (2026-07-11): _on_child_segment_tick gained a `final` kwarg; a final failed tick now WRITES a phase='failed' active_segments_map entry (was: always popped), distinguishing an exhausted-retry failure from a non-final in-progress failure tick (which still pops). New _segment_char_count(segment_id) helper resolves a segment's OWN char count from self._children (never the render-group's combined text_length, per R-G/no-fabrication); every active_segments_map entry now carries a best-effort char_count when resolvable. The as_completed loop's terminal call now passes final=True.
